chunks: What was narrated by ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan, from Ayyūb ibn Nūḥ, from Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a menstruating woman who sweats in her garment. He said: “If it is a garment that clings to her, then I do not like that she should perform salat (prayer) in it until she washes it.”
As for that which indicates that janabah, when it is from what is haram, then the garment is washed from it as a precaution, it is as follows.

key_terms.الْجَنَابَةَ: the state of major ritual impurity
key_terms.تَلْزَمُهُ: it clings closely to her body

ai.seo_question: Can a menstruating woman perform salat (prayer) in a garment she perspired in before washing it?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a legal ruling concerning the garment of a menstruating woman when she has perspired in it. The Imam عليه السلام states dislike for performing salat (prayer) in such a garment until it is washed, and the compiler then transitions to reports concerning janabah from what is haram and washing the garment as a precaution.
